name: substitute in whole file
description: replace every match of <old> with <new> across the file

examples.note: % = all lines, g = every match on each line
add c to confirm each replacement (y/n/a/q)

explanation: Pattern is a regex; escape / inside it or use a different delimiter, e.g. :%s#/usr#/opt#g.
gotchas: without g it only replaces the FIRST match on each line

name: substitute in a visual selection
description: run a substitution only over the lines you selected

examples.note: the ranged-from-visual marks '<,'> are inserted automatically

explanation: Select lines with V, press : and Vim prefills :'<,'> ; type the rest. '<,'> are the visual-start/end marks.

name: delete all lines matching a pattern
description: global command: run :d on every line matching <pat>

examples.note: delete blank lines
g! (or :v) acts on lines that do NOT match

explanation: :g/pat/cmd runs any Ex command on matching lines — e.g. :g/TODO/normal A <-- here.

name: change inner word
description: delete the word under the cursor and enter insert mode

examples.note: change inside the quotes
change inside the parentheses
delete a paragraph (text object 'a paragraph')

explanation: Text objects combine a verb (c=change, d=delete, y=yank, v=select) with i (inner) or a (around) + an object (w word, p paragraph, ( [ { quotes tags). The cursor can be anywhere inside the object.

name: delete (cut) a line
description: delete the current line into the unnamed register

examples.note: delete 3 lines
yank (copy) the line; p pastes below, P pastes above

explanation: dd is really 'cut' — the line goes into a register and can be pasted with p.

name: re-indent the whole file
description: jump to top and auto-indent through to the end

examples.note: gg=top, = reindent operator, G=end
indent current line one shiftwidth; << to outdent

gotchas: = uses the buffer's indentexpr/filetype indent; for code it's only as good as the indent plugin

name: search forward
description: incrementally search for a regex; n/N step through matches

examples.note: then n = next match, N = previous
? searches backward instead
search for the exact word under the cursor (forward)

explanation: Use \v at the start for 'very magic' (PCRE-like) regex: /\v(foo|bar). :noh clears the highlight afterwards.

name: clear search highlight
description: turn off the highlighting from the last search (keeps the pattern)

examples.note: abbreviation of :nohlsearch

explanation: Doesn't unset the pattern, so n still works; it just removes the lingering highlight.

name: undo / redo / repeat
description: u undoes, Ctrl-r redoes, . repeats the last change

examples.note: repeat the last edit — e.g. ciwNEW<Esc> then . on the next word
undo all latest changes on one line

explanation: The dot command . replays the last change operator; pairing it with a motion is the core of efficient Vim editing.

name: yank to the system clipboard
description: copy into the + register so it's available outside Vim

examples.note: yank current line to system clipboard
paste FROM the system clipboard
yank the selection

gotchas: Neovim needs a clipboard provider (wl-clipboard / xclip / xsel) installed for + to work — check with :checkhealth clipboard
* and + differ on X11 (primary vs clipboard); on Wayland/most setups they behave the same

name: record and replay a macro
description: record keystrokes into a register, then replay them

examples.note: qa starts recording into register a; q stops
replay macro a; @@ repeats the last macro
run macro a ten times

explanation: Make the macro end on the same column so it's repeatable; combine with a count or :g for bulk edits.

name: set and jump to a mark
description: drop a named mark, jump back to it later

examples.note: set mark a at the cursor
jump to mark a (exact position); 'a jumps to its line
jump back to where you were before the last jump

explanation: Lowercase marks are per-buffer; uppercase marks (mA) are global across files.

name: navigate the jump list
description: go back (Ctrl-o) and forward (Ctrl-i) through your jump history

examples.note: jump to the previous cursor location (e.g. before a search/G)
jump forward again (Tab is the same key)

explanation: Jumps (searches, G, gg, marks) are recorded; Ctrl-o/Ctrl-i walk that list. gd/gf etc. also push jumps.

name: save and quit
description: the core write/quit Ex commands

examples.note: write (save) without quitting
write and quit (:x/ZZ only write if changed)
quit discarding changes
write-all / quit-all for multiple buffers

gotchas: E212 'can't open file for writing' usually means you need :w !sudo tee % (or open with sudoedit)

name: open / reload a file
description: edit another file, or reload the current one from disk

examples.note: open a file in the current window
reload current file, discarding unsaved changes
open the built-in file explorer (netrw) at cwd

name: switch buffers
description: list open buffers and jump between them

examples.note: list buffers with their numbers
:b takes a number or a name fragment
next / previous buffer
delete (close) the current buffer

name: split windows
description: split the view and move between splits

examples.note: horizontal split (:split); Ctrl-w v = vertical (:vsplit)
move focus left/down/up/right
cycle to the next window; Ctrl-w q closes one
equalise split sizes

name: visual modes
description: select by character, line, or block

examples.note: linewise visual — select whole lines
BLOCK/columnar visual — select a rectangle
insert text on every selected line (column edit)
reselect the last visual selection

explanation: After selecting, apply an operator (d, y, >, c, :s...). Block-visual + I/A is how you edit a column across many lines.

name: jump to a line number
description: move the cursor to line N (or top/bottom)

examples.note: go to line 42
first line / last line
show current line number and file position

name: quick char edits
description: replace one char, join lines, transpose chars

examples.note: replace the single char under the cursor (no insert mode)
join this line with the next (gJ joins without adding a space)
swap the char under the cursor with the next (x deletes, p pastes after)
